Tomato___Early_blight.summary: Early blight is a fungal disease that commonly produces brown, target-like rings with yellow margins.
immediate_actions: Remove and safely dispose of affected crop debris.
Improve airflow and avoid wetting foliage during irrigation.
Ask the local extension service about a crop-registered treatment before applying any product.
prevention: Keep the field free of infected residues.

source.title: Tomato early blight: integrated disease management

Tomato___Late_blight.summary: Late blight can spread rapidly in wet weather and may affect leaves, stems, and fruit.
immediate_actions: Improve drainage and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Remove infected debris and seek local diagnosis promptly.
Use only locally registered control measures after extension advice.
prevention: Monitor closely during cool, wet conditions.

source.title: Tomato late blight: integrated disease management

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial spot causes small water-soaked to brown spots and is difficult to control once established.
immediate_actions: Remove and destroy visibly affected plant parts.
Avoid handling plants when foliage is wet.
Consult the local extension service before choosing a control product.
prevention: Start with disease-free seed and seedlings.
Remove crop residues and volunteer tomato plants.

source.title: Tomato bacterial leaf spot: disease management

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.summary: Tomato mosaic virus can cause mottling, distorted leaves, and stunted growth; it is readily spread by contact.
immediate_actions: Remove symptomatic plants and disinfect hands, tools, and equipment.
Do not handle healthy plants after infected plants without cleaning up.
Consult an agricultural expert to confirm the diagnosis.

source.title: Tomato mosaic virus: symptoms and control

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.summary: Tomato leaf curl is a viral disease associated with whitefly transmission; infected plants should be assessed promptly.
immediate_actions: Remove severely affected plants where recommended by the local extension service.
Monitor and manage whiteflies using locally approved integrated methods.
Remove alternate weed hosts around the field.
prevention: Use yellow sticky traps as part of whitefly monitoring.
Keep field borders and nearby weeds managed.

source.title: Tomato leaf curl and whitefly management

Potato___Late_blight.summary: Potato late blight affects leaves, stems, and tubers and can advance quickly under wet conditions.
immediate_actions: Remove visibly infected plants or parts as advised locally.
Avoid injuring tubers at harvest and do not store visibly infected tubers.
Seek local extension advice on locally registered protective treatment.
prevention: Use crop rotation and maintain drainage.

source.title: Potato late blight: symptoms and management
